subtitle: On the Yamuna’s banks, a kingdom falls and a new road to Delhi opens

panels.shot: wide, split-composition tableau showing Jaichand on an elephant near the Yamuna and Muhammad of Ghor on horseback opposite, storm clouds gathering over the river plain
panels.action: Jaichand Gahadavala rides a caparisoned elephant by the Yamuna’s broad waters while, across a faintly suggested divide of terrain, Muhammad of Ghor sits alert on a warhorse, both kings framed under a darkening sky over the middle Ganga plain.

dialogue.text: In 1194, on the banks of the Yamuna, Jaichand of Kannauj met Muhammad of Ghor—and with their clash, the last great kingdom of the middle Ganga plain broke open the road to a new Delhi.

i18n.hi: ११९४ में, यमुना किनारे कन्नौज के जयचंद की टक्कर ग़ौर के मुहम्मद से हुई—और इस भिड़ंत ने मध्य गंगा के आख़िरी बड़े राज्य को तोड़, नई दिल्ली की राह खोल दी।

panels.shot: slow push-in over a bird’s-eye map of north India, with key centres glowing softly
panels.action: An old parchment map of north India lies spread, the Ganga and Yamuna snaking across it, with Varanasi, Kannauj, Ajmer and Ghazni marked by small stylised palaces glowing faintly in lamplight.

dialogue.text: After Tarain, the map of north India shivered. Chauhans staggered, Ghurid banners edged into the Yamuna, and only one great Hindu court still held the middle Ganga plain—Jaichand’s Kannauj and sacred Kashi.

i18n.hi: तराइन के बाद उत्तर भारत का नक्शा कांप उठा। चौहान लड़खड़ाए, ग़ुरी झंडे यमुना तक सरक आए, और बस एक बड़ा हिंदू दरबार बचा—जयचंद का कन्नौज और पावन काशी।

panels.shot: medium wide inside a palace hall in Varanasi, low-angle on Jaichand on a throne while ministers confer
panels.action: Jaichand Gahadavala, middle-aged and regal, sits on a carved lion-throne in a pillared hall, courtiers and Brahman ministers around him pointing to maps and palm-leaf records, the faint shimmer of the Ganga visible beyond a lattice.

dialogue.text: For decades, the Gahadavalas had poured wealth into temples, ferries and ghats, guarding pilgrim routes and taxes. Jaichand inherited not just a throne, but the last great treasury between the Yamuna and Bihar.

i18n.hi: दशकों से गाहड़वाल मंदिरों, नौकाओं और घाटों पर धन बरसा रहे थे, तीर्थ और कर की राहें थामे। जयचंद को सिर्फ़ गद्दी नहीं, यमुना से बिहार के बीच का आख़िरी बड़ा ख़ज़ाना मिला था।

panels.shot: close medium on Jaichand in private, profile in lamplight, looking toward an unseen west
panels.action: In a quieter chamber, Jaichand stands by an open jharokha, one hand resting on the pommel of his sword, his brow furrowed as he looks toward the imagined west where the sun sets beyond the Yamuna.

dialogue.speaker: Jaichand Gahadavala and Muhammad of Ghor
dialogue.text: Beyond the Yamuna, they say the horsemen of Ghor ride where Rajput spears once stood.

i18n.hi: यमुना के उस पार, कहते हैं अब ग़ौर के घुड़सवार दौड़ते हैं, जहाँ कभी राजपूत भाले खड़े थे।

panels.shot: dynamic low-angle of Muhammad of Ghor in camp, armour half-donned, maps before him
panels.action: Muhammad of Ghor, lean and focused, sits on a low carpet in a military tent, mail shirt partly fastened, one hand tracing a route on a rough map from Ghazni through the Punjab to the Ganga while officers stand attentive.

dialogue.text: From the northwest, Muhammad of Ghor moved with a different gaze. The Punjab had fallen into his net; Tarain had broken Prithviraj. Yet the rich heart of the Ganga plain still lay in Jaichand’s keeping.

i18n.hi: उत्तर-पश्चिम से मुहम्मद ग़ौरी अलग नज़र से बढ़ा। पंजाब उसके जाल में आ चुका, तराइन में पृथ्वीराज टूट चुका। पर गंगा का समृद्ध दिल अब भी जयचंद की मुट्ठी में था।

panels.shot: wide shot of a bustling Gahadavala riverfront, slightly elevated, showing wealth and movement
panels.action: Boats laden with goods crowd a Ganga ghat as tax collectors record cargo, temple towers rise behind them, and Gahadavala soldiers watch, their spears upright, while townsfolk move along the embankment.

dialogue.text: Control of Kashi and Kannauj meant ferries on the rivers, markets on the plains, and the gold of countless pilgrims. To the Ghurid court, chroniclers later wrote, this region gleamed like a casket still unopened.

i18n.hi: काशी और कन्नौज पर पकड़ मतलब नदियों पर नाव, मैदानी हाट, और अनगिनत यात्रियों का सोना। ग़ुरी दरबार के लिए, इतिहासकार लिखेंगे, यह इलाक़ा किसी बंद गहनों के सन्दूक की तरह चमकता था।

panels.shot: low, tense wide of a Ghurid column moving through dust, Muhammad prominent at the front
panels.action: Under a hazy sky, Muhammad of Ghor rides at the head of an armoured cavalry column, dust swirling around swift horses and standard-bearers as they move along a tree-lined track toward the flat riverine horizon.

dialogue.text: Sometime around 1193–94, the Ghurid army turned from the Punjab and Ajmer toward the Ganga. Hasan Nizami would later say their path ran straight for Jaichand’s lands and treasuries.

i18n.hi: ११९३–९४ के आस-पास, ग़ुरी फ़ौज पंजाब और अजमेर से मुड़कर गंगा की ओर चली। हसन निज़ामी लिखता है, उनकी राह सीधी जयचंद की ज़मीनों और ख़ज़ानों पर जा अटकी।

panels.shot: medium shot of Jaichand receiving alarming news from a dusty messenger
panels.action: In a courtyard, Jaichand stands upright as a dusty messenger bows, pointing westwards with urgency, while attendants holding spears look on with unease.

dialogue.text: News rode ahead of hooves: towns in the west shaken, roads cut, Ghurid scouts seen near the Yamuna. No chronicler records Jaichand’s exact council that day, but the outcome is clear—he marched to meet them.

i18n.hi: घोड़ों से पहले ख़बरें दौड़ीं: पश्चिम के क़स्बे दहल गए, रास्ते कटे, ग़ुरी जासूस यमुना किनारे दिखे। किसी इतिहास ने उस दिन जयचंद की सभा नहीं लिखी, पर नतीजा साफ़ है—वह ख़ुद निकल पड़ा।

panels.shot: expansive wide shot along the Yamuna near Chandawar, both armies facing across slight undulations
panels.action: On an open plain by the gleam of the Yamuna, Jaichand’s line of elephants and infantry ranks face Muhammad’s massed cavalry and archers, banners flickering as morning mist clings low to the grass.

dialogue.text: Near Chandawar, by the Yamuna’s bend, the two forces met. Persian chroniclers remember the field as another Tarain, but this time the foe was not a Chauhan neighbor, and the river left little room to retreat.

i18n.hi: चंदावर के पास, यमुना की मोड़ पर दोनों सेनाएँ भिड़ीं। फ़ारसी लेख इसे एक और तराइन कहते हैं, पर इस बार दुश्मन चौहान पड़ोसी नहीं था और नदी ने पीछे हटने की जगह ही न छोड़ी।

panels.shot: low-angle close medium on Jaichand atop his elephant, looking over his army
panels.action: Jaichand stands in howdah armour atop a war elephant, calm but intent, right hand raised as he surveys his lines stretching across the plain, the Yamuna glinting beyond his shoulder.

dialogue.speaker: Jaichand Gahadavala and Muhammad of Ghor
dialogue.text: Hold the line. The river is our witness; let it not see us falter.

i18n.hi: पाँति थामो। नदी साक्षी है, इसे हमें डगमगाते न देखना पड़े।

panels.shot: dynamic mid-wide of Muhammad signaling the charge, arrows already in the air
panels.action: Muhammad of Ghor, face set, raises his arm in signal as mounted archers loose a first dark cloud of arrows, their horses springing forward toward the distant silhouettes of elephants.

dialogue.text: Hasan Nizami places Muhammad in the thick of the fight, urging his cavalry against the Gahadavala center. The chronicles praise his resolve, for their audience was his court, but through them a pattern emerges.

i18n.hi: हसन निज़ामी मुहम्मद को जंग के बीच दिखाता है, घुड़सवारों को गाहड़वाल के केंद्र पर धकेलते हुए। तारीख़ें उसके हौसले की तारीफ़ करती हैं, और इन्हीं से एक ढाँचा उभरता है।

panels.shot: chaotic but non-graphic wide of the battlefield, elephants turning, cavalry wheeling
panels.action: The field at Chandawar roils with movement: elephants sway and begin to turn, infantry press around them, and Ghurid horsemen dart between gaps, lances lowered, as the Yamuna lies broad and indifferent in the background.

dialogue.text: Elephants, once symbols of steadiness, could become islands of panic when lines wavered. Somewhere amid that dust and shouts, the Gahadavala formation broke—and with it, a century of their dominance.

i18n.hi: हाथी, जो कभी ठहराव की निशानी थे, पंक्तियाँ डगमगाएँ तो घबराहट के टापू बन गए। धूल और नारों के बीच कहीं गाहड़वाल की क़तार टूटी—और उसके साथ उनकी सदियों की बादशाहत।

panels.shot: somber close on Jaichand mid-battle, partially obscured by dust and silhouettes, his face tense
panels.action: Through dust and blurred forms of soldiers, Jaichand is seen in three-quarter profile on his elephant, jaw set, gaze intense, as the scene around him tilts toward disorder.

dialogue.text: Later storytellers would argue over his final moments—cut down in the crush, or lost in the river. The chronicles agree on one stark point: Jaichand did not return from Chandawar.

i18n.hi: बाद के किस्सागो उसकी आख़िरी घड़ी पर भिड़ते रहे—भीड़ में कटा या नदी में डूबा। पर एक बात पर सब तारीख़ें सहमत हैं: जयचंद चंदावर से कभी लौट न पाया।

panels.shot: wide, quiet aftermath of the battlefield with distant Ghurid standards and abandoned equipment
panels.action: Under a calmer sky, the battlefield lies strewn with dropped shields and overturned standards; in the distance, Ghurid banners stand upright while small groups of soldiers move methodically among the spoils.

dialogue.text: Hasan Nizami writes of plunder taken, of elephants and treasure seized. The details serve his patron, but the silence of Gahadavala inscriptions after this year marks an echoing fact: their line, as a power, ends here.

i18n.hi: हसन निज़ामी हाथियों, माल और लूट के ढेर लिखता है। बातें उसके सरपरस्त की हैं, पर इस साल के बाद गाहड़वाल की शिलालेख चुप हो जाते हैं—यहीं उनकी सत्ता की रेखा टूटती है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Muhammad of Ghor in camp at dusk, reflective, with scribes nearby
panels.action: Muhammad of Ghor sits at ease but alert on a carpet outside his tent at dusk, a scribe writing nearby, as he looks toward the east where the sky still glows above the unseen Ganga plain.

dialogue.text: From Chandawar, the road lay open to the Ganga’s rich cities. Ghurid authority, once a frontier force, could now plant garrisons, levy taxes, and stitch a chain of strongholds that future Sultans would call their base.

i18n.hi: चंदावर से गंगा के समृद्ध नगरों की राह खुल गई। ग़ुरी हुकूमत, जो कल तक सरहद की ताकत थी, अब क़िले बिठा सकती थी, कर उठा सकती थी, और वह कड़ी बुन सकती थी जिसे आगे के सुल्तान अपना आसरा कहेंगे।

panels.shot: sweeping bird’s-eye over Varanasi and Kannauj under new garrisons, with mosques and temples both visible
panels.action: From high above, the cityscapes of Varanasi and Kannauj are shown in sequence: temple spires and old palaces now share the skyline with new fortified enclosures and simple mosque courtyards, soldiers of the new regime visible at key gates.

dialogue.text: Power shifted, but life along the rivers did not vanish. Temples, markets, caravanserais—many endured, now feeding different treasuries. The Yamuna and Ganga watched one court fall and another take its place.

i18n.hi: ताकत बदली, पर नदियों की ज़िंदगी नहीं मिटी। मंदिर, बाज़ार, सराय—कई जस के तस रहे, बस अब दूसरे ख़ज़ाने भरते। यमुना और गंगा ने एक दरबार गिरते, दूसरा उठते देखा।

panels.shot: medium shot centuries later of a bard reciting to villagers, Jaichand’s image on a cloth painting behind
panels.action: In a later village scene, a bard stands before a small crowd, gesturing dramatically, while behind him a painted cloth shows a stylised Jaichand on an elephant facing a foreign horseman.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, village tales would recast Jaichand as foil or betrayer in the story of Prithviraj, folding him into legend. Yet the records place him not as traitor, but as the last great king to stand on this frontier.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद, गाँव की कहानियाँ जयचंद को पृथ्वीराज की दास्तान में ख़लनायक या गद्दार बना देंगी। पर दस्तावेज़ उसे गद्दार नहीं, इस सरहद पर खड़ा आख़िरी बड़ा राजा दिखाते हैं।

panels.shot: tranquil wide of the Yamuna near Chandawar in the present, with faint ghostly silhouettes of armies in the sky
panels.action: The Yamuna flows quietly past the Chandawar region under a soft modern sky, farmers working its banks, while faint, translucent silhouettes of elephants and horsemen seem to rise from the haze above the water.

dialogue.text: On this quiet bend of the Yamuna, a battle once rewrote India’s map. Jaichand’s fall reminds us that history turns not on one ‘traitor’ or one charge, but on the slow work of roads, treasuries and the wars that seize them.

i18n.hi: यमुना की इस शांत मोड़ पर कभी एक जंग ने भारत का नक्शा बदल दिया था। जयचंद का पतन याद दिलाता है कि इतिहास किसी एक ‘गद्दार’ या एक धावे से नहीं, बल्कि राहों, ख़ज़ानों और उन पर टूटी जंगों से करवट लेता है।

title_i18n.en: The Last King on the Yamuna

subtitle_i18n.en: On the Yamuna’s banks, a kingdom falls and a new road to Delhi opens
subtitle_i18n.hi: यमुना किनारे एक राज्य ढहता है, दिल्ली को नई राह खुलती है
